- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates drop; adjust downward by 3–7% to match true decline.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 5 days, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast change by 1–2 days or smooth transition.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show mean reversion (price moving back toward 60–70% of 30-day moving avg), model often fails to recognize; force forecast to align with recent 10-day mean.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 30-day moving average of history, adjust forecast to match historical volatility pattern (e.g., if history shows 3–5% volatility, don’t exceed ±5% from avg).
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often overfits short-term noise; use 10-day rolling average to filter out erratic spikes.
